explanation: If you must drive in reverse, you should first walk around the vehicle to check for hazards in your path of travel. Make frequent use of the mirrors on both sides of your vehicle while backing. Always back up as slowly as possible.

question: A pre-trip inspection should include:
option_a: A check of the engine oil level.
option_b: Removing coolant.
option_c: Spraying WD-40 into the air filter.
option_d: Removing a tire.
explanation: A pre-trip inspection should include a check of components in the engine compartment, including a check of the engine oil level.

question: If a bus is disabled while passengers are still on board:
option_a: Another bus should push the disabled bus to its destination.
option_b: The bus should be towed to its destination.
option_c: The passengers should be asked to push the bus.
option_d: The bus may need be towed to the nearest safe location to discharge the passengers.
explanation: A bus that is disabled while passengers are on board should not be towed or pushed, unless it is absolutely necessary. If needed, the bus should be towed or pushed only as far as the nearest safe location for the passengers to be discharged.

question: When should you check and adjust your mirrors?
option_b: While driving
option_c: After a trip
option_d: Mirrors do not need to be adjusted.
explanation: The adjustment of mirrors must be checked prior to the start of any trip.

question: During the pre-trip vehicle inspection test:
option_a: Applicants will not have to identify the ABS.
option_b: Windshield wipers are not to be addressed.
option_c: Shock absorbers only need to be checked on one axle.
option_d: The steering box should be checked for leaks.
explanation: During the external inspection portion of the pre-trip vehicle inspection test, you must verify that the steering box is securely mounted and not leaking.

question: A vehicle inspection:
option_b: Is helpful in identifying minor issues before they become major problems.
option_c: Should not be done by the driver.
option_d: Should be performed once a month.
explanation: A vehicle should be inspected before every trip to help ensure that any small mechanical issues are caught before they become more serious problems. It is better to discover a problem with your vehicle before a drive than after the drive has begun.

question: If a tire fails, you should:
option_b: Stay off the brakes.
option_c: Swerve.
option_d: Wave your arms at other drivers.
explanation: Using the brakes after a tire failure could cause you to lose control of your vehicle. Unless you're about to hit something, stay off of the brake until the vehicle has slowed sufficiently.

question: When traction is poor, a driver should accelerate slowly:
option_a: Because it is best to always accelerate very slowly.
option_b: So they do not lose control of their vehicle.
option_c: So the driver does not accelerate faster than the vehicle ahead.
option_d: To be the last vehicle through an intersection.
explanation: Speeding up too quickly on a road with poor traction could cause a driver to lose control of their vehicle. In conditions that cause poor traction, a driver should accelerate especially smoothly and gradually.

question: Water on bridges:
option_a: Usually freezes before water on other parts of a roadway.
option_b: Usually freezes after water on other parts of a roadway.
option_c: Will not freeze.
option_d: Is not a concern in cool weather.
explanation: Bridges will generally freeze before other parts of the roadway. Be careful on bridges when temperatures are around the freezing point.

question: To prevent fatigue while driving, you should:
option_b: Keep the cab cool.
option_c: Keep the cab poorly ventilated.
option_d: Close the vents.
explanation: A hot, poorly-ventilated area can make a person sleepy. Opening a window, opening a vent, or using the air conditioning can help keep the cab cool and reduce the risk of fatigue.

question: Brake pads should:
option_b: Be covered with oil.
option_c: Be covered with brake fluid.
option_d: Not have any oil or grease on them.
explanation: When inspecting your brakes, you should verify that the shoes and pads do not have any oil, grease, or brake fluid on them.

question: When using mirrors while driving, you should:
option_b: Look in the mirrors for extended periods of time.
option_c: Use only the rearview mirror.
option_d: Use only the driver’s side mirror.
explanation: Focusing on your mirrors for too long can be dangerous because you will have traveled a substantial distance without looking at the road ahead.

question: When approaching a railroad crossing, a driver should:
option_b: Expect to hear a train.
option_c: Cross the tracks before an approaching train reaches the crossing.
option_d: Reduce their speed.
explanation: You should approach every railroad crossing with the expectation that a train is coming. Do not rely on signals or your hearing to reliably tell you if a train is present. Always slow down when approaching a crossing. Never try to race a train.

question: During the vehicle inspection test, you will be required to do all of the following, except:
option_b: Point to or touch each item.
option_c: Explain what you are checking and why.
option_d: Crawl under the vehicle.
explanation: As a part of earning your CDL, you will have to pass an inspection test and demonstrate that your vehicle is safe for operation. During the vehicle inspection test, you will have to walk around the vehicle and point to or touch each item and explain to the examiner what you are checking and why. You will not have to crawl under the hood or under the vehicle.

question: Which of the following is not an example of a driving hazard?
option_b: An open road
option_c: A police car assisting a motorist on the side of the road
option_d: An ice cream truck
explanation: Passing an accident scene can be hazardous because the people involved in the accident may not be watching traffic, and the scene itself may distract other passing drivers. Ice cream trucks can create hazardous conditions because they attract children who may not pay attention to nearby vehicles. Shoppers near the roadway are often paying attention to stores, not passing traffic.

question: How should you check your hydraulic brakes?
option_a: Pump the brakes three times, then apply firm pressure to the brake pedal for five seconds. The brake pedal should not move.
option_b: Pump the brakes three times, then apply firm pressure to the brake pedal for five seconds. The brake pedal should slowly move toward the floor.
option_c: Pump the brakes three times, then apply firm pressure to the brake pedal for five seconds. The brake pedal should slowly rise.
option_d: Pump the brakes three times, then apply firm pressure to the brake pedal for five seconds. The brake pedal should be easy to push to the floor.
explanation: To test hydraulic brakes, you should pump the brake pedal three times, then apply firm pressure to the brake pedal and hold for five seconds. The pedal should not move. If it does, there may be a leak.

question: When driving on packed snow, you should reduce your speed:
option_b: By about one-third.
option_c: By about one-quarter.
option_d: By about one-eighth.
explanation: When driving on packed snow, you should reduce your speed by one-half or more. It can be difficult to stop or turn when operating on a slippery surface, so you must adjust your speed to drive safely under such conditions.

question: When passing another vehicle, you should:
option_a: Make eye contact with the other driver.
option_b: Assume the other driver doesn’t see you.
option_c: Honk your horn.
option_d: Wave to other drivers.
explanation: It is always safest to assume that other drivers, bicyclists, and pedestrians don't see you. Be prepared for the possibility that they may suddenly move into your path. It may be safe to lightly tap your horn or flash your lights as you pass.

question: Texting while driving a CMV is:
option_a: Acceptable if the text is work-related.
option_b: Acceptable if there are fewer than 10 words in the text message.
option_c: Encouraged because it is safer than talking on the phone.
option_d: Prohibited.
explanation: Texting while driving a commercial motor vehicle is both illegal and dangerous. Manually entering text into or reading text from any electronic device is considered texting.

question: A fatigued driver:
option_b: Should take over-the-counter remedies to wake them up.
option_c: May make critical decisions too slowly.
option_d: Is usually more conscientious than a typical driver.
explanation: If you are fatigued, you will not see or react to hazards as quickly as you would if you were fully energized and awake. You will be impaired in making critical decisions.

question: To help your vehicle be seen by others:
option_b: Your lights should be off during the day.
option_c: Your lights should be covered with grease.
option_d: Your lights should only be used in the rain.
explanation: When driving at night, it is important that your lights be clean so that they provide as much light as possible. This will help others to see your vehicle.

question: When driving, keeping space between your vehicle and other vehicles is:
option_b: Important.
option_c: A waste of time.
option_d: Optional.
explanation: For the safety of everyone on the road, it is essential that you maintain adequate cushions of space between your vehicle and other vehicles. This will help ensure that if you need to stop your vehicle, you will be able to do so without hitting someone else.

question: You should always be able to stop within:
option_b: 1,000 feet of your vehicle.
option_c: Your view of the road ahead.
option_d: 30 seconds of hitting the brakes.
explanation: You should always make sure that your vehicle will be able to stop within the area of the road that you are able to see. This means that you must slow down whenever conditions reduce visibility.

question: A sign that your vehicle's brakes will need repair is that the:
option_a: Brake pads are not covered in grease.
option_b: Brake pads are not covered in oil.
option_c: The brake pads are worn thin.
explanation: Potential problems to check for when inspecting brakes include cracked drums; shoes or pads with oil, grease, or brake fluid on them; and shoes that are missing, broken, or worn dangerously thin.

question: If driving a vehicle with a manual transmission, you can prevent your vehicle from rolling backward when starting from a stop by:
option_a: Partly engaging the clutch before removing your foot from the brake pedal.
option_b: Placing the vehicle in reverse before moving forward.
option_c: Fully engaging the clutch before removing your foot from the brake pedal.
option_d: Placing the vehicle in neutral before moving forward.
explanation: To prevent rolling backward when starting from a stop, you should partly engage the clutch before removing your foot from the brake. Apply the parking brake whenever necessary to prevent your vehicle from rolling back.

question: During a trip, carry-on bags should be:
option_b: Left near the doorway.
option_c: Stacked behind the driver.
option_d: Secured to allow the driver to move freely.
explanation: Bus passengers must not be allowed to leave baggage in doorways or aisles during a trip. Baggage and freight must be secured in a way that will allow the driver to move freely and easily; allow riders to exit by any window or door in an emergency; and protect riders from injury if items fall or shift.

question: When planning to drive a bus that has been parked for a few days:
option_a: The driver should assume the interior is in good working order.
option_b: The driver should call the local police department.
option_c: The driver should do a walkthrough inspection to ensure no damage has occurred since the last trip.
option_d: The driver should ask the passengers to check the interior of the bus.
explanation: People sometimes damage unattended buses. Before driving a bus that has been unattended, you should check the interior to confirm that everything is in proper condition.

question: The minimum tread depth of all major grooves on tires that are not on the front of a CMV should be a minimum of:
option_b: 2/32 of an inch.
option_c: 4/32 of an inch.
option_d: 3/4 of an inch.
explanation: When inspecting your tires, verify that there is at least 4/32 of an inch of tread depth in every major groove on the front tires, and tread depth of at least 2/32 of an inch on the other tires. Tires on the same vehicle should all be the same size.

question: When inspecting the engine compartment, you should not:
option_b: Check the coolant level in the radiator.
option_c: Drain the brake fluid.
option_d: Check the windshield washer fluid level.
explanation: When inspecting the engine compartment, you should check the oil level, coolant level, and windshield washer fluid level, among other things.

question: If you are approaching a drawbridge that does not have a signal light or traffic control attendant, you should:
option_a: Continue across the drawbridge with caution.
option_b: Speed up to get across the drawbridge as quickly as possible.
option_c: Wait for another driver to cross first.
option_d: Stop, look, and make sure the bridge is completely closed before proceeding.
explanation: A bus should always stop at any drawbridge that is not controlled by a signal light or traffic control attendant. Stop at least 50 feet before the draw of the bridge, and make sure that it is completely closed before crossing.

question: If a person is boarding a bus while carrying a container of gasoline, the driver should:
option_a: Place the gasoline container near the back of the bus.
option_b: Keep the gasoline container near the front of the bus.
option_c: Place the gasoline container in the aisle.
option_d: Not allow the gasoline container onto the bus.
explanation: A bus driver should not allow passengers to bring common hazards, such as gasoline or car batteries, onto their bus.

question: Before driving, access panels should be:
option_b: Removed.
option_c: Stored inside the storage compartment.
option_d: Closed.
explanation: You should always inspect the outside of your bus before driving. During this inspection, make sure to close all emergency exits and access panels.

question: A curve's posted design speed is:
option_b: Safe for all vehicles, including buses.
option_c: The minimum speed at which the curve should be driven.
option_d: Not always safe for buses.
explanation: Even under ideal weather conditions, a bus being driven at the posted design speed for a curve could either roll over or slide off the road. For safety, you should reduce your speed before driving a bus around a curve.

question: Carry-on bags should be secured:
option_a: In front of the back door.
option_b: In front of the front door.
option_c: In a location that allows access to all emergency exits.
option_d: On top of the bus.
explanation: Bus passengers must not leave luggage in doorways or aisles. All items should be secured in a way that allows passengers to exit by any door or window in an emergency.

question: When inspecting the interior of a bus, you should:
option_a: Not waste time looking at the handrails and floor lining.
option_b: Make sure the seats are loosely secured.
option_c: Assume all buzzers work properly.
option_d: Make sure emergency exits are easy to use.
explanation: When inspecting the interior of a bus, you must make sure everything is safe and in proper working condition. Make sure emergency exits are properly marked and easy to use.

question: If a bus has a brake and accelerator interlock system, the system should:
option_a: Be turned off in most situations.
option_b: Only be used in inclement weather.
option_c: Never be used in place of the parking brake.
option_d: Operate the rear door.
explanation: Urban transit buses may have a brake and accelerator interlock system, which applies the brakes and holds the throttle in an idle position while the rear door is open. This system should not be used as a substitute for the parking brake.

question: The standee line is:
option_a: A line that passengers must stand behind.
option_b: A line that passengers must stand on.
option_c: A line that should be used as passengers exit the bus.
option_d: A line on the outside of a bus.
explanation: On a bus designed to carry standing passengers, no passengers may stand in front of the rear of the driver's seat. Any such bus must have a line on the floor, or some other marking, that indicates where passengers may not stand. This is called a standee line.

question: On a bus, the driver:
option_a: Does not need to wear a seat belt.
option_b: Must always wear a seat belt.
option_c: Must wear a seat belt, but only during usual school hours.
option_d: Must wear a seat belt, but only if they have been licensed for less than a year.
explanation: The driver's seat of a bus should be equipped with a seat belt, which must always be used by the driver.

question: The driver’s seat of a bus should include:
option_a: A pocket for storage on its left side.
option_b: A pocket for storage on its right side.
option_c: A seat belt.
option_d: A cup holder.
explanation: The driver's seat on a bus must be equipped with a seat belt, which the driver should always use.

question: When arriving at a destination, it is best to remind exiting passengers to take their carry-on bags with them:
option_b: After you stop the bus.
option_c: At least five times.
option_d: As they exit the bus.
explanation: Before a bus is brought to a complete stop at its destination, it is best for the driver to remind exiting passengers to take their carry-ons with them.

question: One reason for you to sign a previous driver’s vehicle inspection report is if:
option_a: The previous driver dated their entry.
option_b: Reported defects are certified to have been repaired.
option_c: You plan to drive for longer than one hour or travel farther than 50 miles.
option_d: The report is left on the dashboard.
explanation: You should only sign a previous inspection report if defects were either noted and certified to have been repaired or if repairs were not needed.

question: If driving a charter bus, a driver should:
option_a: Tell passengers how to operate the TVs, if equipped.
option_b: Not allow passengers to board until the scheduled departure time.
option_c: Allow passengers to board early to get ahead of schedule.
option_d: Tell passengers to fill the back of the bus first.
explanation: To help prevent theft or vandalism, charter bus drivers should not allow passengers to board the vehicle until the scheduled departure time.

question: Before driving a bus that has been left unattended:
option_a: The vehicle should be thoroughly washed.
option_b: Air should be removed from tires.
option_c: The interior should be checked for damage.
option_d: The driver should look for any animals that may have gotten onboard.
explanation: People sometimes damage unattended buses. When inspecting a bus that has been left unattended, you should do a walkthrough to check the interior for damage.

question: When carrying multiple classes of approved hazardous materials on a bus, no more than a combined total of ____ of the materials may be transported at once.
option_b: 50 pounds
option_c: 100 pounds
option_d: 500 pounds
explanation: Buses may carry no more than 500 total pounds of hazardous materials, including no more than 100 pounds of any one class of material.

question: When approaching a drawbridge that is controlled by a traffic signal, you may proceed:
option_b: Only after coming to a complete stop 50 feet before the bridge.
option_c: Only if other vehicles are also proceeding.
option_d: Only after getting out of your vehicle to check the conditions.
explanation: If approaching a drawbridge that is controlled by a traffic signal displaying a green light, you may slow down and proceed without stopping.

question: Bus accidents most frequently occur:
option_b: On highways.
option_c: On rural roads.
option_d: In parking garages.
explanation: Bus accidents most commonly occur at intersections. Use special caution when driving where you may encounter an increased number of vehicles and pedestrians.

question: Buses should never transport:
option_b: Small arms ammunition.
option_c: Emergency hospital supplies.
option_d: Radioactive materials.
explanation: Buses must never transport labeled radioactive materials in the space occupied by people. Small arms ammunition labeled ORM-D, emergency hospital supplies, and medications are allowed.

question: Before operating a bus, you should ensure that it is safe by:
option_a: Reviewing the inspection report left by the previous driver.
option_b: Kicking the tires.
option_c: Asking your supervisor if the bus seems safe.
option_d: Asking passengers if they are comfortable.
explanation: A bus must always be inspected before it is driven. The inspection process must include a review of the inspection report made by the previous driver. You should operate the vehicle only if defects listed on the inspection report have been certified as repaired or as not needing to be repaired.

question: A bus driver does not need to stop when approaching:
option_b: A streetcar crossing.
option_c: A railroad crossing.
option_d: A stop sign.
explanation: When approaching a railroad crossing while driving a bus, you must stop between 15 and 50 feet from the nearest track to look and listen for any approaching trains. Only proceed once you are certain that there are no approaching trains. You do not need to stop at streetcar crossings; if a police officer or flagger is directing traffic; if there is a green traffic signal at the crossing; or at crossings marked "exempt" or "abandoned."

question: Keeping emergency equipment on a bus is:
option_b: Encouraged, especially if there is extra room on the bus.
option_c: Encouraged if there are more than 15 passengers present.
option_d: Required by law.
explanation: Commercial vehicles must be equipped with the appropriate emergency equipment. Equipment should include a fire extinguisher, emergency reflectors, and spare fuses, if applicable.

question: If feeling sleepy while driving, you should:
option_a: Press on and finish the trip.
option_b: Drive faster to arrive to your destination sooner.
option_c: Leave the road and take a nap.
option_d: Take an energy pill.
explanation: If you begin to feel sleepy while driving, the only safe response is to stop driving and get some sleep. Attempting to fight off exhaustion is dangerous and a major cause of fatal crashes. Stimulants are not a safe solution because they may help keep you awake but will not make you more alert. Once stimulants wear off, you will be even more tired than you were originally.

question: Federal and state laws require:
option_a: Drivers to regularly inspect their vehicles.
option_b: Drivers to inspect their vehicles, but only if they believe there may be a problem.
option_c: Drivers to inspect their vehicles if planning to travel out-of-state.
option_d: Drivers to inspect their vehicles, but only if they will be transporting hazardous materials.
explanation: Commercial drivers are required by federal and state laws to inspect their vehicles before every trip. Regular inspections can help drivers identify issues before they become dangerous and costly.

question: As part of the vehicle inspection test, a CDL applicant may be asked to:
option_b: Replace a tire.
option_c: Remove the alternator belt.
option_d: Replace spark plugs.
explanation: While testing for a CDL, an applicant will be required to go through a full vehicle inspection. The vehicle inspection test will include an engine oil level check.

question: An example of mandatory emergency equipment is:
option_a: A supply of spare electrical fuses.
option_b: A loud horn.
option_c: A battery-operated flashlight.
option_d: A supply of fireworks.
explanation: Mandatory emergency equipment includes: at least one fire extinguisher; spare electrical fuses (unless the vehicle is equipped with circuit breakers); and warning devices for parked vehicles (such as reflective triangles).

question: Which of the following is not a sign of fatigue?
option_b: Daydreaming
option_c: Yawning repeatedly
option_d: Drifting from your lane
explanation: Driving while fatigued is dangerous. Warning signs of fatigue include difficulty focusing; repeated yawning or rubbing of the eyes; daydreaming or wandering thoughts; and drifting out of your lane.

question: Most heavy vehicles require ____ to change gears.
option_b: Double shifting
option_c: Triple clutching
option_d: Triple shifting
explanation: Most heavy vehicles with manual transmissions require double clutching to change gears. A driver should release the accelerator, push in the clutch, and shift into neutral at the same time. After releasing the clutch and allowing the vehicle to change to the necessary speed, the driver should push in the clutch, shift gears, then simultaneously release the clutch and accelerate.

question: When traveling with cargo, you must make sure the cargo is secure:
option_b: Every 150 miles or three hours of driving.
option_c: Only after traveling up a hill.
option_d: Only after coming to a hard stop.
explanation: Cargo should be inspected before beginning a trip, within the first 50 miles of the trip, and every three hours or 150 miles traveled. The driver of a truck transporting cargo is responsible for the cargo being safely secured throughout the trip.

question: What is black ice?
option_a: A thick layer of ice on the road
option_b: A thin layer of ice on the road
option_c: Ice that is black from debris on the road
option_d: Ice that is easily seen
explanation: Black ice is a thin layer of ice that is clear enough for the road surface to be seen through it. A road covered in black ice may look like it is merely wet.

question: Mirror adjustment can only be checked properly if:
option_b: There is no trailer attached to the tractor.
option_c: The vehicle is on a slight incline.
option_d: The vehicle is on a slight decline.
explanation: If a trailer is attached to a tractor, the adjustment of the vehicle's mirrors can only be checked accurately if the trailer is straight.

question: Which of the following surfaces provides the least amount of traction?
option_b: Ice that is wet
option_c: Wet pavement
option_d: Dry pavement
explanation: Be especially cautious when driving on ice that has begun to melt. Ice that is wet is much more slippery than ice that is dry.

question: When starting the vehicle during the pre-trip inspection, the coolant temperature should:
option_b: Rise slowly.
option_c: Hold steady.
option_d: Jump quickly.
explanation: After starting your vehicle during the pre-trip inspection, you should watch the gauges. The coolant temperature should gradually rise to a normal operating range.

question: When exiting your vehicle, you:
option_a: Must maintain four points of contact with the vehicle.
option_b: May turn to face the road before your exit is complete.
option_c: Must be facing away from the vehicle.
option_d: Must be facing the vehicle.
explanation: When exiting your vehicle during the basic vehicle control skills test, you must face the vehicle and maintain three points of contact at all times. If your testing vehicle is a bus, you must maintain contact with the handrail. Exiting the vehicle incorrectly may result in automatic failure of the basic control skills test.

question: When inspecting the exhaust system, which of the following should not cause concern?
option_b: Loose or broken mounting brackets
option_c: Leaking exhaust system parts
option_d: Exhaust system parts that are not rubbing against fuel system parts
explanation: When inspecting a vehicle's exhaust system, be alert to a number of potential problems, including loose, broken, or missing exhaust pipes, mufflers, tailpipes, or vertical stacks; loose, broken, or missing mounting brackets, clamps, bolts, or nuts; exhaust system parts rubbing against fuel system parts, tires, or other moving parts of the vehicle; and exhaust system parts that are leaking.

question: Distracted drivers may be:
option_b: Traveling at consistent speeds.
option_c: Preoccupied with using their cell phones.
option_d: Not talking to anyone else in their vehicles.
explanation: You may be able to tell that another driver is distracted if you can see them drifting within a lane or across lane dividers; traveling at inconsistent speeds; being preoccupied with a cell phone, a map, food, or other items; or engaging in conversation with passengers.

question: The front of an enclosed trailer should:
option_b: Contain rags.
option_c: Not be used for cargo.
option_d: Be free of cracks.
explanation: When inspecting an enclosed trailer as a part of the vehicle inspection test, check the front area of the trailer for signs of damage, such as cracks, bulges, or holes.

question: When approaching a curve during the on-road driving test, you must do all of the following, except:
option_a: Check traffic thoroughly in all directions.
option_b: Reduce your speed before entering the curve.
option_c: Keep your vehicle in its lane.
option_d: Steadily use the brakes throughout the curve.
explanation: When approaching a curve during the on-road driving test, you should thoroughly check traffic in all directions. Before entering the curve, reduce your speed sufficiently so that further braking or shifting is not required. Keep your vehicle in its lane and continue checking traffic in all directions.

question: Which of the following is not acceptable emergency equipment?
option_b: Six fuses
option_c: Three liquid burning flares
option_d: Four yellow squares
explanation: During the vehicle inspection test, you will need to show emergency equipment, including spare electrical fuses; three red reflective triangles, six fuses, or three liquid burning flares; and a properly charged and rated fire extinguisher.

question: If an aggressive driver is involved in a crash on the road ahead of you, you should:
option_a: Block the driver in with your vehicle.
option_b: Stop after the crash scene and report the driver’s aggressive behavior to the police.
option_c: Continue driving and mind your own business.
option_d: Pull over and yell at the driver.
explanation: If you observe a crash involving an aggressive driver, you should stop a safe distance from the crash scene, wait for police to arrive, and inform them of the aggressive behavior you witnessed.

question: If pulled off to the side of the road, you should:
option_a: Allow your taillights to alert other motorists.
option_b: Turn on your emergency flashers to warn other motorists.
option_c: Keep your lights off to avoid distracting other motorists.
option_d: Keep your door open to warn other motorists.
explanation: If you must stop and park on the side of the road, make sure to turn on your emergency flashers. This is especially important at night. Taillights are not an adequate when alerting other drivers because the drivers may mistakenly think your vehicle is moving normally and collide with it.

question: Drivers are usually the least alert:
option_b: In the early evening.
option_c: Late at night.
option_d: In the afternoon.
explanation: Drivers are usually less alert when driving at night, especially after midnight.

question: The maximum amount of play that is safe on a 20-inch steering wheel is:
option_b: Two inches.
option_c: 10 inches.
explanation: A steering wheel with play of more than 10 degrees may be defective. On a 20-inch wheel, this is equal to about two inches of movement at the rim of the wheel.

question: During exercises that are not the straight line backing exercise, you may exit your vehicle to check its position no more than:
option_b: Two times.
option_c: Three times.
option_d: Four times.
explanation: A driver is allowed to exit their vehicle to check its position during any basic control skills test exercise. This action is called a "look." During the straight line backing exercise, a driver may not exceed one look. During any other exercise, a driver may not exceed two looks.

question: During the driving test, when encountering a railroad crossing, you should:
option_a: Pass another vehicle on the tracks if the other vehicle is going too slow.
option_b: Get out of the vehicle to check for a train.
option_c: Not change gears while your vehicle is on the tracks.
explanation: During the on-road driving test, do not stop, change gears, pass another vehicle, or change lanes while any part of your vehicle is in a railroad crossing.

question: Fueling a bus while passengers are on board is:
option_b: Acceptable only on trips of more than 100 miles.
option_c: Acceptable only if doing so is unavoidable.
explanation: A bus should not be refueled while passengers are on board unless it is absolutely necessary to do so. In particular, a bus with riders on board should never be refueled inside an enclosed building.

question: Which of the following is not a sign of a person being drowsy?
option_b: Drifting from your lane
option_c: Feeling hungry
option_d: Yawning
explanation: Driving drowsy is dangerous and should always be avoided. Warning signs of drowsiness include frequent blinking, your eyes closing or going out of focus by themselves, frequent yawning, and drifting between lanes.

question: A pre-trip inspection:
option_a: Should never be completed the same way two times in a row.
option_b: Should always be completed in the same order.
option_c: Should only be done if it is sunny outside.
option_d: Should not be done if the driver thinks the vehicle is in good operating order.
explanation: A pre-trip inspection should be completed in the same way before every drive. Consistency will help you learn all of the proper steps and decrease the likelihood that you will forget to check something.

question: When crossing railroad tracks, you should:
option_b: Change gears.
option_c: Try to pass.
option_d: Stay in your lane.
explanation: When crossing railroad tracks during the on-road driving skills test, you must not stop, switch gears, pass another vehicle, or change lanes while any part of your vehicle is in the crossing.

question: During the skills test, if making a turn that requires a stop, you should:
option_b: Stop after the stop line to get a better view.
option_c: Allow your vehicle to roll.
option_d: Keep the front wheels aimed straight ahead.
explanation: If you must come to a stop before making a turn during the driving skills test, you should come to a smooth stop behind any stop line, crosswalk, or stop sign. Keep your front wheels aimed straight ahead and do not let your vehicle roll. If stopping behind another vehicle, stop where you are still able to see the rear tires of the vehicle ahead of you.

question: If the brakes “pull” to one side or the other when you use them, it's a sign that:
option_b: The brakes need to be checked.
option_c: The brakes are new.
option_d: The brakes have too much stopping power.
explanation: If your vehicle "pulls" to one side when braking, you may have brake trouble. If there is an issue with your brakes, you should fix the issue before driving. Operating an unsafe vehicle is against federal and state laws.

question: Once stopped as part of the stop/start maneuver, you should:
option_b: Keep the vehicle in first gear.
option_c: Be perpendicular to the curb.
option_d: Be blocking a driveway.
explanation: When parking as a part of the stop/start maneuver during the on-road driving skills test, you must apply the parking brake. The gears should be shifted into neutral or park. You must be parked parallel to the curb and should not be blocking any driveways or intersections.

question: When trying to put out an electrical fire, you should:
option_b: Use a B:C extinguisher.
option_c: Use an X extinguisher.
explanation: B:C fire extinguishers are designed to work on electrical fires and burning liquids. Don't pour water on an electrical fire.

question: While driving, a driver should:
option_a: Not be concerned with what is happening on the sides of their vehicle.
option_b: Be concerned with what is happening on all sides of the vehicle.
option_c: Not be concerned with what is happening behind the vehicle.
explanation: It is essential that you are aware of what is happening on all sides of your vehicle at all times. Scan the road ahead and make regular checks of the mirrors on both sides of your vehicle while you are driving.

question: While driving, gauges are:
option_b: Unpredictable.
option_c: To be monitored for potential signs of trouble.
explanation: While driving, you should watch your vehicle's gauges for signs of trouble. Be sure to inspect your gauges before beginning a trip to ensure that they are in proper working order.

question: As part of a pre-trip inspection, you should look for all of the following, except:
option_a: Tires with too much air pressure.
option_b: Tires with too much wear.
option_c: Tires made by different manufacturers.
explanation: When inspecting your tires, verify that there is tread depth of at least 4/32 of an inch in every major groove on the front tires and tread depth of at least 2/32 of an inch in grooves on the other tires. Be sure that your tires are not too worn, are not cracked, have proper air pressure, and are all equally sized.

question: In an emergency situation, you should:
option_b: Not always respond by stopping.
option_c: Never respond by swerving.
option_d: Always turn on your flashers to warn other drivers.
explanation: Stopping is not always the safest option when responding to an emergency while driving. It is usually safer to steer out of the way when attempting to avoid a crash.

question: In very hot weather, tires should be checked regularly because:
option_b: Air pressure may increase with the temperature.
option_c: The tread wears down more quickly than in cooler weather.
explanation: Because air pressure increases with temperature, you should pay special attention to the tire mounting and pressure when traveling in hot weather.

question: When completing an offset back/left parking maneuver, a driver should:
option_a: Pull straight forward, then back to the left.
option_b: Drive straight back, then pull forward to the left.
option_c: Pull straight forward, then drive straight back.
explanation: If you are asked to complete an offset back/left parking maneuver, you should first pull straight forward, then back up to the left. Your vehicle must be parked completely within the boundaries of the parking space.

question: When drivers turn, they usually:
option_a: Look in the direction of the turn.
option_b: Look in the direction opposite the turn.
option_c: Look behind their vehicles.
explanation: When turning, drivers usually look in the direction of their turn. If a driver fails to signal before a turn or lane change, their body movements may still provide a clue that they are planning to turn.

question: A standee line on a bus:
option_a: Marks where riders may not stand.
option_b: Is useful to get passengers to board and exit the bus.
option_c: Is a part of the air conditioning system.
explanation: On a bus designed to carry standing passengers, no passengers may stand in front of the rear of the driver's seat. Any such bus must have a line on the floor, or some other marking, that indicates where passengers may not stand. This is called a standee line.

question: During the vehicle inspection test, you will be asked to:
option_b: Explain to the examiner what you would inspect and why.
option_c: Estimate the weight of a load in a trailer.
option_d: Change a windshield wiper.
explanation: During the CDL vehicle inspection test, you must be able to inspect your vehicle and explain to the examiner what you are inspecting and why.

question: When exiting a vehicle, a driver should:
option_a: Hop directly from their seat to the ground.
option_b: Maintain at least one point of contact with their vehicle.
option_c: Be turned to face their vehicle.
explanation: When exiting your vehicle during the basic vehicle control skills test, you must face the vehicle and maintain three points of contact at all times. If your testing vehicle is a bus, you must maintain contact with the handrail. Exiting the vehicle incorrectly may result in automatic failure of the basic vehicle control skills test.

question: Before a bus enters a curve, the driver should:
option_b: Not change their speed.
option_c: Reduce their speed.
explanation: Buses should always enter curves at reduced speeds. A driver should be especially cautious if entering a curve under wet or slippery conditions.

question: Poisonous fumes can enter a cab due to:
option_b: Using the wrong type of fuel.
option_c: A lack of oil in the engine.
explanation: A faulty exhaust system is a serious safety hazard. It may allow poisonous fumes to enter the vehicle's cab or sleeper berth.

question: Hydroplaning:
option_a: Only occurs at extremely high speeds.
option_b: Can occur at speeds as slow as 30 mph.
option_c: Happens most frequently when tire pressure is too high.
option_d: Happens most frequently when tires have good tread.
explanation: If there is enough water on the road, hydroplaning can occur at speeds as low as 30 mph. It is most likely if the tires' air pressure is too low or if tires' tread is worn.

question: A jogger wearing a stereo headset:
option_a: Is probably aware of what is happening around them.
option_b: May not be aware of what is happening around them.
option_c: Can hear the sounds of traffic.
explanation: Be careful around pedestrians, joggers, and cyclists who are wearing headphones. They may be unable to hear your vehicle approaching and may do dangerous things because they do not know you are there.

question: Looking far ahead of your vehicle while driving is:
option_a: Discouraged, as there is little you can do about something far up the road.
option_b: Encouraged to help you identify hazards as early as possible.
option_c: Not permitted.
explanation: Good drivers look down the road at least 12 to 15 seconds ahead of their vehicles. This makes it possible to identify hazards early, when drivers are more likely to have time to respond appropriately.

question: Regrooved tires:
option_a: Should not be used on any vehicle.
option_b: Should not be used on the front of a bus.
option_c: Should not be used on trucks hauling gravel.
explanation: Regrooved, recapped, or retreaded tires are prohibited on the front wheels of a bus.

question: If the coolant temperature gauge goes above the highest safe temperature, you should:
option_b: Pull over and figure out what's wrong.
option_c: Run the air conditioner.
explanation: If the coolant temperature gauge goes above the highest safe temperature, you should stop driving as soon as possible and try to figure out what is wrong. There could be an issue in your vehicle that could lead to engine failure and possibly a fire.

question: When backing with a trailer:
option_a: You should not back up in a straight line.
option_b: You should not correct drift until you are far off course.
option_c: You should frequently pull forward to reposition the vehicle.
explanation: When backing, you should pull forward to reposition your vehicle whenever needed. Drift should be corrected immediately by turning the steering wheel in the direction of the drift.

question: If a truck is equipped, a trailer brake hand valve can be used to:
option_b: Prevent the truck from rolling back when being started from a stop.
option_c: Check the engine oil level.
explanation: If a tractor-trailer is so equipped, the trailer brake hand valve can be used to stop the vehicle from rolling back when being started from a stop.

question: Aggressive driving is:
option_a: Operating a vehicle in a selfish or pushy manner.
option_b: Operating a vehicle with a strong regard for other motorists’ safety.
option_c: Operating a vehicle in the left lane.
explanation: Aggressive driving is the act of operating a motor vehicle in a selfish, bold, or pushy manner and without regard for the rights or safety of other road users.

question: When checking power steering hoses during a pre-trip inspection, you should look for:
option_b: Secure connections to the battery.
option_c: Extra hose pieces available for repairs.
explanation: When doing a pre-trip inspection on a vehicle with power steering, be sure to check the hoses, pumps, and fluid level. In particular, you should check the hoses for leaks.

question: When driving on packed snow, you should reduce your speed by:
option_b: About one-third.
option_c: About one-quarter.
explanation: Reduce your speed when traveling on surfaces that provide reduced traction. Reduce your speed by one-half or more when traveling on packed snow.

question: Which of the following is acceptable if found during a pre-trip inspection?
option_b: Tread of 3/32 of an inch in the grooves of the front tires
option_c: Tires manufactured by different makers
explanation: When inspecting your tires, verify that there is at least 4/32 of an inch of tread depth in every major groove on the front tires, and tread depth of at least 2/32 of an inch on the other tires. Tires on the same vehicle should all be the same size.

question: The use of a hand-held mobile device while driving is:
option_b: Acceptable if weather conditions are clear.
option_c: Permitted if use is work-related.
explanation: Using a hand-held mobile telephone while operating a CMV is both illegal and dangerous.

question: What is the best way to stop if your brakes fail while you are driving downhill?
option_b: Let the vehicle slow down on its own.
option_c: Let rumble strips slow your vehicle.
explanation: If your brakes fail on a downgrade, you will need to quickly find something outside that can stop your vehicle. An escape ramp is the best option. If no escape ramp is available, use the least hazardous available option, such as driving into an open field or side road that flattens out or turns uphill.

question: When backing with a trailer, you should begin by:
option_a: Turning the steering wheel in the direction of the turn.
option_b: Turning the steering wheel in the direction opposite of the turn.
option_c: Turning the wheel as sharply as possible.
explanation: When backing with a trailer, begin by turning the steering wheel in the direction opposite of the turn. Once the trailer starts to turn, reverse the direction of the steering wheel to follow the trailer.

question: When near a railroad crossing:
option_a: You should expect to hear every approaching train.
option_b: You may not hear a train, even if one is approaching.
option_c: You will hear two short blasts of a train's horn if a train is approaching.
explanation: You should never assume that you will hear an approaching train. The train operator may fail to sound the horn, or the use of a train's horn may be prohibited in a specific area. Even if the train does sound its horn, noise from inside your own vehicle may prevent you from hearing the train until it is dangerously close.

question: After two violations of any state law regarding hand-held mobile phone use:
option_a: You will need to cancel your mobile phone service.
option_b: Your CDL will be disqualified.
option_c: You will be required to drive 10 mph under the posted speed limit for a period of time.
explanation: If you are twice convicted of violating any state law regarding hand-held mobile phone use, your CDL will be disqualified. Consequences will become more severe with subsequent violations.

question: Shortly after a tire has been changed, you should:
option_a: Stop to make sure the lug nuts are still tight.
option_b: Repair the brakes.
option_c: Deflate the tire to 10 psi.
explanation: After a tire has been changed, you should stop a short while later to recheck the tightness of the lug nuts.

question: If you are being tailgated while driving a large vehicle, do all of the following, except:
option_b: Increase your following distance.
option_c: Increase your speed.
explanation: If you find yourself being tailgated by another driver, you should increase your following distance and avoid making quick moves. Increasing your speed may only result in the other driver continuing to tailgate you at a higher speed. Do not turn on your taillights or flash your brake lights at the other driver.

question: When starting from a stop:
option_a: A vehicle should shift to the right.
option_b: A vehicle should be put into third gear.
option_c: A vehicle should not roll back.
explanation: To avoid hitting anything behind you, make sure that your vehicle does not roll back when you start from a complete stop.

question: The more alcohol in the body:
option_a: The quicker the liver will digest the alcohol.
option_b: The less effect the alcohol will have on the individual.
option_c: The longer it will take to remove the alcohol from the body.
explanation: The body removes alcohol at a fixed rate. The more alcohol consumed, the longer it will take for the body to remove the alcohol from its system.

question: What does the vehicle inspection report do?
option_a: Inform the motor carrier about problems that may need fixing
option_b: Ensure that the vehicle is inspected regularly
option_c: Keep people accountable for inspecting the vehicle
explanation: A vehicle inspection report keeps the carrier informed about any problems that need to be fixed.

question: Broken suspension parts:
option_b: Should be repaired, but not immediately.
option_c: Cannot be identified.
explanation: The suspension system performs the vital functions of holding up the vehicle and its load while keeping the axles in place. Defects in the suspension are therefore extremely dangerous.

question: When traveling down a steep grade, you switch into a lower gear:
option_b: When you have already started the grade.
option_c: As far down the grade as possible.
explanation: You should shift your vehicle's transmission into a low gear before staring a downhill grade. Be prepared for gravity to increase your vehicle's speed when traveling downhill.

question: When driving a bus with passengers, you should:
option_a: Not engage in conversation with the passengers.
option_b: Fuel the bus with the passengers on board.
option_c: Push a stranded vehicle.
explanation: To reduce the risk of distraction, bus drivers should not engage in conversation with passengers. Avoid fueling a bus while passengers are on board. Do not tow or push a disabled bus with riders aboard the vehicle, unless it would be unsafe for the passengers to exit the bus at the location where it has stalled.

question: Bridges usually freeze:
option_a: Only once temperatures drop significantly below 32 degrees Fahrenheit.
option_b: After all other surfaces.
option_c: Before other surfaces.
explanation: Bridges tend to freeze before other parts of the roadway. Be particularly careful on bridges when temperatures are close to the freezing point.

question: How should you brake if your vehicle's ABS is not working?
option_a: Brake normally, as you will still have functioning brakes.
option_b: Pump the brake repeatedly.
option_c: Press the brake pedal down as hard as you can.
explanation: Without a working Anti-Lock Braking System (ABS), your vehicle will still have normal brake function. Continue to drive and brake as you normally would and have your ABS serviced as soon as possible.

question: A danger of looking at your mirrors for too long is that:
option_b: You will travel too far without knowing what is happening on the roadway ahead.
option_c: The mirrors may shake and move.
explanation: Looking at your mirrors for too long is dangerous because you may travel a substantial distance without knowing what is going on ahead of you. It is important to be aware of your surroundings in all directions.

question: Which of the following is not a cause of hydraulic brake failure?
option_b: Brake fade on long hills
option_c: Downshifting
explanation: Most cases of hydraulic brake failure come from one of two causes. The brakes may fail due to a loss of hydraulic pressure or due to overuse on long hills, causing the brakes to fade.

question: Emergency equipment in a vehicle is:
option_a: Only required for vehicles that are transporting hazardous materials.
option_b: Only required during interstate travel.
option_c: Required.
explanation: During a pre-trip inspection, you should check for emergency equipment, including spare electrical fuses; three red reflective triangles, six fuses, or three liquid burning flares; and at least one properly charged and rated fire extinguisher.

question: Rough acceleration:
option_a: Is a good way to stay awake on long trips.
option_b: Is distracting.
option_c: Can cause mechanical damage.
explanation: Rough acceleration can cause mechanical damage, so be sure to accelerate smoothly and gradually.

question: A ramp's posted speed limit:
option_b: Is suitable for some vehicles, but may be too fast for a large CMV.
option_c: Is just a suggestion and may be exceeded.
explanation: Posted speed limits on exit and entrance ramps often show speeds that are safe to be driven by cars. However, these speed limits may be too fast for large or heavily-loaded vehicles and CMV drivers will likely need to slow down to a speed below the posted limit.

question: If you are transporting a drunk passenger, you should:
option_a: Force them to immediately exit the bus.
option_b: Wait until you are at an appropriate area, such as a stop or well-lit area, to have them exit the bus.
option_c: Give them coffee to help them sober up.
explanation: If a passenger is drunk and disruptive, you are still responsible for their safety. They should be discharged in a safe location, which may be the next scheduled stop or another well-lit area where other people are present.

question: During a trip, gauges are:
option_b: The only way a driver can learn of potential trouble with the vehicle.
option_c: A way to learn of potential trouble with the vehicle.
explanation: During a trip, you should regularly check the gauge and instrument panels, mirrors, tires, cargo, and lights for signs of trouble.

question: You are especially likely to encounter strong winds when:
option_b: Going into tunnels.
option_c: Driving on shoulders.
explanation: Strong winds can make it difficult to keep a vehicle in its proper lane. Strong wind can be a particular problem when a vehicle is being driven out of a tunnel.

question: When approaching a railroad crossing, a bus driver should:
option_a: Stop the bus between 15 and 50 feet from the nearest track.
option_b: Drive cautiously, but not stop the bus unless a train is coming.
option_c: Speed up to ensure the bus has momentum to cross the tracks.
explanation: When approaching a railroad crossing, bus drivers should stop their vehicle between 15 and 50 feet from the nearest track and look both ways for a train. The driver should not proceed until they are certain no trains are approaching.

question: To avoid a collision with a hazard on the roadway:
option_a: You should always try to stop.
option_b: Swerving may be a safer option than stopping.
option_c: You should never swerve.
explanation: Swerving out of the way of a hazard is sometimes safer than trying to stop before reaching the hazard. You can usually turn away from something more quickly than you can come to a complete stop.

question: When inspecting your vehicle, you should check for all of the following, except:
option_a: Too much air pressure in your tires.
option_b: Too little air pressure in your tires.
option_c: A consistent name brand across all of your tires.
explanation: During a pre-trip inspection, you should verify that the air pressure is neither too low nor too high in any of your tires.

question: Before operating a bus, you should make sure that the:
option_a: Floor lining is easy to remove.
option_b: Handrails are attached loosely.
option_c: Emergency exits are properly marked.
explanation: When inspecting the interior of a bus, you must make sure everything is safe and in proper working condition. Make sure emergency exits are properly marked and easy to use.

question: Shaded areas of a road:
option_b: Are usually blocked from all moisture, so they cannot freeze.
option_c: Will remain slick after ice has melted on other areas of the road.
explanation: Because they are exposed to less sunlight and warm up more slowly, shaded areas will remain icy and slippery after ice on other areas of the road has melted.

question: If a vehicle's Anti-Lock Braking System (ABS) is malfunctioning:
option_a: The vehicle will have no brakes.
option_b: The vehicle will still be able to brake.
option_c: The vehicle will likely travel faster than usual.
explanation: An Anti-Lock Braking System (ABS) intervenes to reduce brake pressure if there is a risk of wheel lockup. If the ABS isn't working, the vehicle's basic braking functions are not affected. A driver should continue to drive and brake in a normal manner.

question: Radial and bias-ply tires:
option_b: Should be used together on the front of a vehicle.
option_c: Should not be used together.
explanation: Radial and bias-ply tires should not be used together. All wheels on a vehicle should be the same style and equally-sized.

question: Roof hatches on buses:
option_b: Must always be closed when driving.
option_c: May be locked in a partially-opened position.
explanation: On a bus, it is acceptable to lock some roof hatches in a partially-opened position to provide fresh air, but this should not be made a regular practice. Remember that opening these hatches will slightly increase a bus's clearance.

question: If there is a fire in your vehicle and you are not sure how to extinguish it, you should:
option_b: Try douse the flames with water.
option_c: Move away from the flames and wait for the firefighters.
explanation: If you are not sure which method to use when putting out a fire, do not attempt to extinguish the fire on your own. Instead, wait for firefighters to arrive and let them handle it. This is especially true if you are experiencing a hazardous materials fire.

question: If your brakes fail when traveling downhill, decide what to do as quickly as possible because:
option_a: The longer you wait, the faster your vehicle will go.
option_b: The longer you wait, the more vehicles will get out of your way.
option_c: The longer you wait, the slower your vehicle will go.
explanation: However you choose to deal with a brake failure on a downhill slope, it is important that you make your decision as quickly as possible. The longer you wait to act, the faster your vehicle will be moving, and the harder it will become to stop.

question: Hydroplaning usually occurs:
option_b: When driving at speeds slower than 15 mph.
option_c: In areas where water collects on the road.
explanation: Hydroplaning occurs on surfaces where water has collected. If there is enough water, vehicles can hydroplane at speeds as low as 30 mph. Hydroplaning becomes more likely if tires are under-inflated or if the tread is worn.

question: A stopped bus:
option_a: Is not a cause for concern since it is stopped.
option_b: Is only a concern if passengers are exiting the bus.
option_c: Is a concern whether or not passengers are visible.
explanation: You should always exercise caution when driving near a stopped bus. There could be passengers in the vicinity and the bus may either prevent them from seeing you or you from seeing them.

question: If a vehicle is power steering-equipped, the hoses should be:
option_b: Securely connected to the battery.
option_c: Carrying fuel.
explanation: When inspecting a vehicle equipped with power steering, you should inspect the hoses, pumps, and fluid levels. Specifically check the hoses for leaks.

question: Banked curves:
option_b: Can be taken at any speed without concern.
option_c: Should be avoided.
explanation: Banked curves have posted safe design speeds. These posted speeds may be safe to be driven by cars but may be unsafe to be driven by larger vehicles, like buses and trucks.

question: After picking up passengers at a stop, a driver should:
option_a: Allow the passengers time to sit or brace themselves before beginning to drive.
option_b: Honk their horn and re-enter traffic.
option_c: Begin driving as quickly as possible.
explanation: You should start and stop as smoothly as possible to help prevent passenger injury. After passengers have boarded your bus at a stop, you should allow them time to be seated or to brace themselves before you begin driving.
